whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text:
Hello, my name is Emma Hendry. My piece is called Forest Fire. I conceived of it around
the time when there is forest fires happening on the West Coast, kind of all over the world,
and people were calling them megafires. I saw all these photography of the entire setting being
this orange glow and how forest fires kind of affect the light spectrum to block the other
colors and just sort of create this almost sunset look. It's super eerie and I immediately thought
that the red neon has a really similar look to it. I hand bent all the neon tubes and had them
bombarded with neon and traced each piece and had a vector file that I made
to make it look like a red neon. I made a vector file that I made to make it look like a red neon.





I made a vector file that I made to have each of these pieces of acrylic laser cut on.
And although you don't really see the orange glow in the darkness, I think it gives it
some dimension and reflection and it changes when you turn the lights on or in a medium light
rather than a dark light. My practice is being a sculptor. I've also been designing and managing
custom lighting. That includes like floor lamps and chandeliers and sconces and
working with lighting for my job and just working in those categories.
I think sometimes influences how I think formally of sculptures. So they're trees but they also
are sort of the proportions of like a floor lamp and so they almost have sort of like an
industrial or commercial quality to them which plays into the concept of how all these different
different factors can contribute to ecological disasters.
And I've worked with neon in other capacities and it's sort of all led up to my biggest installation.
I'm not sure if you can see the installation yet.
